messages.subject: Syntax highlighting with text where one of the quotation marks is off the screen
messages.subject_clean: Syntax highlighting with text where one of the quotation marks is off the screen
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I wanted to ask about this minor issue I have. Whenever there is some text in the code, but one of the quotation marks is off the screen, then the syntax highlighting erroneously believes the text starts at the second quotation mark. E.g., say you have:

x <- "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod
tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam,
***quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo
consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum
dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident,
sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum."

y <- runif(10)
nchar(x)
# Etc.

Say the top of the screen is at ***, then the second " will be interpreted (apparently) as the first quotation mark, and the subsequent lines shown in the colour corresponding to character text. Moving up and down the screen eventually fixes that.

Do you know if this is specific to vim-r-plugin, or more generally an issue of syntax highlighting in vim?

Many thanks!

messages.body_plain:
This happens because there is no "syntax sync" in syntax/r.vim. I just added "syntax sync minlines=40" to syntax/r.vim (at github). This might solve the specific problem reported, but may also make syntax highlight for R slow, specially if fold is enabled. Users can control the value of minlines by setting the value of r_syn_minlines in their vimrc. Example:

let r_syn_minlines = 400

messages.subject: Send file: no stopping with error warning!
messages.subject_clean: Send file: no stopping with error warning!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jakson!

Is possible send file without it stops with error messages? If not, and if it would be possible, would be interesting to implement this command. Why? Sometimes we have huge scripts in which we need to perform only part of it. Part of this depends on other objects previously created. I came across this problem now. I just need to adjust some graphics for publication that are in an big code. Obviously this code is derived from analyzes in which there are attempts to adjustments for a particular purpose. When this adjustment does not occur, the messages appear as usual in R. Therefore, I have to send line by line all the code to be able to reach my goal. The command "send file" would be solution the problem if it would stop in the middle of the error messages.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Send file: no stopping with error warning!
messages.subject_clean: Send file: no stopping with error warning!
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, but I don't know how to do what you want with R scripts: the Vim-R-plugin sends to R the command base::source() to evaluate the whole R script, and source() doesn't have any argument to ignore errors.

When the plugin was in its early stages of development, multiple lines of code were sent directly to R Console instead of being sourced, but sometimes the code was either incompletely or incorrectly pasted in the R console.

messages.subject: RDSendSelection etc. for Python?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is it possible to use the same remapped key-bindings (as suggested in the doc) for Python? I.e., have

vmap <Space> <Plug>RDSendSelection
nmap <Space> <Plug>RDSendLine

also work when using Python (or any other interpreter) instead of R?

Thanks!
